evidence.field: 形義通解: graphic formation and evolution
evidence.text: The entry analyzes oracle-bone 生 as 屮 (a sprout) above 一 representing ground, expressing a plant growing out of earth. It says early bronze forms continue the oracle-bone structure; a dot was later added beneath 屮 as a decorative stroke and then became a horizontal stroke, making it resemble 土. Seal script retains the sprout-emerging-from-ground idea. The entry treats Shuowen’s gloss 進也 as an extended sense, rather than the graphic core.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：生

evidence.text: The entry cites oracle-bone examples: 合集34078 uses 生 in a prayer for childbirth; 合集8648正 生月 is interpreted as the following month; 合集116正 uses 生 adjectivally of fresh/live birds; 合集10270 refers to a live deer. These show early uses, but the entry’s proposed semantic connection between the following-month sense and life/growth is an interpretation, not a demonstrated chronological derivation.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：生

evidence.field: 形義通解: bronze and Warring States uses
evidence.text: For bronze inscriptions, the entry cites 生 meaning give birth in 叔尸鐘, occur/produce in 中山王方壺, living in 中方鼎, lifespan in 蔡姞簋, and as a phonetic loan for 姓 on 兮甲盤. It cites Warring States manuscripts for childbirth in 清華簡二《繫年》 and living opposed to dying in 上博竹書一《緇衣》 slip 19. The cited examples establish attested uses; they do not by themselves order all senses into a chronology.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：生

evidence.text: The related 姓 entry says 生 supplies sound in 姓, alongside 女 in oracle-bone forms and 人 in bronze forms; it also reports that oracle-bone 生 can be read as 姓 in 多生, while giving 多甥 as an alternative proposal. This is a whole-graph phonetic borrowing/use and is distinct from 生’s role as a complete graph. No component-level phonetic analysis applies to 生 itself here.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：oracle-piece entry for 生 and 姓

evidence.source: 許慎《說文解字》, as transcribed in 漢語多功能字庫
evidence.text: The entry transcribes 說文:「進也。象艸木生出土上。凡生之屬皆从生。」The historical lexicographic account describes plants emerging above soil; the modern paleographic entry interprets 進 as an extended sense. Shuowen is a historical source and does not independently prove every detail of the earlier oracle-bone structure.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：生

evidence.source: Che-mao Tsai, Institute of History and Philology, Academia Sinica
evidence.field: article metadata and abstracted discussion of 生月
evidence.text: Tsai’s 1993 article record identifies the study as 卜辭生字再探, published in Bulletin of the Institute of History and Philology 64.8, pp. 1047–1076. The accessible page discusses disagreement over 生月: it presents the established ‘following month’ analysis and argues from lunar waxing/waning, while other readings have taken 生月 as ‘this month’ or questioned the reading. This is a disputed lexical interpretation; it does not establish the character’s graphic origin.
evidence.title: 卜辭生字再探 A New Look at the Character ‘sheng’ in Oracle Bone Inscriptions

evidence.source: Che-mao Tsai, Fudan University Center for Unearthed Documents and Paleography
evidence.text: Tsai argues that oracle-bone 生月 means the next month, relating it to the moon beginning to grow again, and rejects an alternative reading of the month graph as 夕 in the cited context. The argument concerns interpretation of an oracle-bone phrase; it is not proof that ‘next month’ was the earliest meaning of 生.
evidence.title: 蔡哲茂：卜辭生字再探

evidence.text: Unicode describes its Unihan lookup as the means to retrieve individual ideograph properties, including readings, by code point, and identifies the current lookup dataset as Unicode 18.0.0. The character-specific GetUnihanData URL was attempted but returned an internal error during this research. The supplied local Unihan row records kMandarin 生 = shēng; this is a local dataset observation, not an independently verified character-specific web result.
evidence.title: Unihan Database Lookup

evidence.source: Local data supplied in research input; Baxter–Sagart 2014 table
evidence.text: The supplied local rows give 生 modern pinyin shēng; Baxter–Sagart Middle Chinese sraeng (also srjaeng in one row); Old Chinese *sreŋ, with row-specific glosses ‘bear, be born; live’ and ‘fresh, raw’ and explicit uncertainty in one row (*sreŋ (MC srj- > sr-; or *s.reŋ ?)). These notations are preserved as distinct table fields/rows. No phonetic component claim is made for 屮 or 一. The upstream Baxter–Sagart page was attempted but not accessible; these rows are local evidence only.
evidence.title: Old Chinese: A New Reconstruction (Baxter–Sagart)

evidence.field: 生 detailed senses and historical citation examples
evidence.text: The entry separates growth, giving birth/raising, living opposite death, and producing/occurring into separate senses, illustrating them with citations to classical works including 詩, 左傳, 論語, 孫子, and 孟子. This lexicographic list documents later lexical range but is not used to infer chronological order among senses.
evidence.title: 生 shēng - 漢典

search_audit.query: 生 Mandarin shēng Unihan U+751F; 生 屮 pronunciation Old Chinese *sreŋ Baxter Sagart 屮; 生 oracle bone 生月 多生 debate 蔡哲茂 字義; 生 character Shuowen 進也 original meaning birth grow oracle bone evidence
search_audit.outcome: Confirmed Unicode lookup documentation and opened competing discussion of the oracle-bone 生月 phrase. The character-specific Unihan endpoint and Baxter–Sagart upstream site returned internal errors. CNS official character data displays modern 國語 shēng, but did not provide the requested Unicode Unihan record.

gaps: The official character-specific Unicode Unihan record at https://www.unicode.org/cgi-bin/GetUnihanData.pl?codepoint=751F could not be opened; the local kMandarin row 生 = shēng is provided but cannot be presented as an inspected official character page. The base Unihan lookup documentation was inspected.

The Baxter–Sagart upstream resource was inaccessible. The exact 生 rows were supplied from sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv and have been preserved as local notation; no character-specific external verification was possible.

No kMandarin row for 屮 was supplied or externally verified, and no 屮 reconstruction rows were supplied. Thus no component-to-host sound comparison is asserted. 屮 is treated only as the graphically meaningful sprout component in the CUHK account, not as a phonetic component.

Dossier mentions conservative form 𤯓 and calls it unrelated to 㞷 or 𡴀; inspected references did not establish that detailed comparison or independently establish the form’s chronology/corruption history.

CUHK reports several Shang oracle-bone usages and cites inscription numbers, but the accessed text does not date individual inscription artifacts. A date for each quoted token is therefore not assigned.

生月’s interpretation is contested, and proposed readings include ‘next month’ versus ‘this month’; the scholarly debate does not demonstrate an ordered semantic transition from plant growth to month terminology.

The sources do not give a securely dated chain for semantic changes from plant growth to birth, life, freshness/rawness, or lifetime. Those senses are reported independently where attested rather than arranged as a chronology.
No bulk reuse terms for the recurrent dictionary databases were verified. No extract is recommended; character-specific paraphrase and citations suffice.
